title: "Instructions for coding agents working with ANS question banks"
subtitle: "Format, build, import and checks, as settled by test imports (University of Amsterdam, September and October 2026)"
date: "16 October 2026"
---

*People, read [README](README.html) first. This file is written for a coding agent (Claude Code
or similar) and is meant to be read in full before any ANS work.*

You are helping a teacher write, convert, build or check questions for **ANS** (ans.app), a
digital assessment platform. Questions are written as text files in the R/exams format and built
into a QTI 2.1 package with `tools/build-ans.R`, which ANS imports. Read this file completely
before you read, convert or build any ANS question. Section 10 says what is verified and what is
not; when something is untested, say so to the teacher instead of assuming it works.

The folder `examples/` holds 12 working questions (3 exercises). When in doubt about the format,
copy the example that looks most like what you need.

## 1. Rules that matter most

1. **Import QTI 2.1 packages through the button "QTI 2.X package (Legacy)".** The Respondus CSV
   route gives no grading criteria, no penalty for wrong ticks in multiple-response questions,
   and only alphanumeric gaps. QTI 3.0 loses the text, links, figures and model answers around
   fill-in parts. (Verified, four import rounds.)
2. **Write only elements ANS itself emits.** One unexpected element can sink the whole package
   with "There are no exercises to import". When in doubt, copy the structure of an item from
   the teacher's own QTI 2.X export. The builder already writes the right form; do not hand-edit
   its XML.
3. **Never put a scorer rubric inside the `itemBody` of a fill-in question.** ANS imports it as
   question text, so students see the answer. (Verified.)
4. **One answer field per question.** Several gaps in one question are possible in ANS's own
   multi-gap form (section 6.3), but ANS imports those gaps as alphanumeric gaps that accept only
   the exact keys, so give each numeric answer its own question. Otherwise make the parts separate
   questions of one exercise (section 2.4).
5. **List images and data files as `<file>` entries of the item that uses them** in the manifest.
   A separate manifest resource per file makes ANS create an empty exercise titled
   `d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e`. (Verified.)
6. **Multiple-response (tick-all) questions need at least one true statement**, and the stem must
   say so ("Check the statement(s) that is/are true; at least one statement is true."), because
   ANS's correction for guessing assumes it. The builder stops otherwise.
7. **Compute every key from the data, in code.** Never copy a number from a published answer, a
   textbook or a previous version of the question without recomputing it. Published answers
   contain errors.
8. **Check every import by exporting again and comparing** (section 8). You cannot import
   yourself; the teacher imports and gives you the re-export.

## 2. The question format

One file per question, `.qmd` or `.Rmd`, in R/exams markdown. Number the files, because the build
order is the sorted file order (`1-spider-a-test.qmd`, `1-spider-b-hypotheses.qmd`, ...).
Every file has these sections, in this order.

- `Question` (what students see), with an `Answerlist` for the options or one empty line per gap;
- `Solution` (the model answer), with an `Answerlist` of `True.` / `False.` per option in choice
  questions;
- `Meta-information` (type, key, points, title).

An R chunk before `Question` may compute or simulate anything the question needs; inline
`` `r value` `` puts its values in the text. Give it `#| include: false` when it only computes.

### 2.1 Single choice

```markdown
Question
========
Stem text. State alpha whenever the answer depends on it.

Answerlist
----------
* Correct option
* Wrong option (a mistake you can name)
* Wrong option (another nameable mistake)

Solution
========
Why the first option is right, then one line per wrong option naming its mistake.

Source line, for example: DSUJ §9.9, p. 384.

Answerlist
----------
* True.
* False.
* False.

Meta-information
================
exname: short-unique-id
extype: schoice
exsolution: 100
exshuffle: TRUE
exextra[anstitle]: Title shown in ANS
```

Write the correct option first; `exshuffle: TRUE` shuffles once at build time, so every student
sees the same order unless ANS's own setting shuffles per student.

### 2.2 Tick-all (multiple response)

As single choice, with `extype: mchoice`, one `1` per true statement in `exsolution` (for
example `1100`), and the stem ending with "Check the statement(s) that is/are true; at least one
statement is true." ANS scores each true statement +1/k and each false one -1/(n-k).

### 2.3 Numeric gaps

One gap is `extype: num` with `exsolution` and `extol` (the margin). The gap's label is a
one-line `Answerlist` in the question; the builder stops on a gap without a label.

```markdown
Question
========
What does the model predict for a cat owner? Use two decimals.

Answerlist
----------
* Predicted life satisfaction:

Solution
========
...

Meta-information
================
exname: short-unique-id
extype: num
exsolution: 60.13
extol: 0.01
exextra[anstitle]: Title shown in ANS
```

Several gaps in one question use `extype: cloze` with `##ANSWER1##`, `##ANSWER2##`, ... in the
text. The text right before each placeholder is its label. Give one empty `Answerlist` line per
gap, `exclozetype: num|num`, `exsolution: -2.47|11`, `extol: 0.01|0`, and `expoints` **per gap**
(two gaps worth 1 point together need `expoints: 0.5`). `exextra[alt]: 2.47|` adds accepted
answers per gap (spaces between answers, `|` between gaps), for example the other sign of t
where the sign only reflects the order of the variables.

In a `cloze`, the builder also adds the obvious variants of each numeric key (a comma decimal,
no leading zero) and writes the margin as a `low;high` range, as ANS's own exports do. A single
`num` gap stays a float with a tolerance, which ANS imports as its numeric gap with that margin;
no variants are added there.

**Caution, seen on import in October 2026:** ANS imports the gaps of a multi-gap question as
alphanumeric gaps, not as numeric gaps with the margin. They then accept only the exact keys, and a
key such as `-3.10` is stored as `-3.1`, so a student who types `-3.10` is marked wrong. For numeric
answers, give each gap its own question (one `num` gap each, parts of one exercise), or set the gaps
to *Numeric* with a margin by hand after import.

### 2.4 Multi-part exercises

One file per part, all with the same `exextra[exercise]` and the same `exextra[anstitle]`, named
so they sort next to each other. Part 1 carries the shared scenario and the data link; ANS shows
it inside question a. Do not label parts a), b); ANS letters them itself. A part can be any type,
with its own points. R/exams weaves every file on its own, so numbers shared between parts are
recomputed or repeated in each part. ANS shuffles **exercises**, never the parts within one, so
"the data from the previous question" only works within one exercise.

### 2.5 Open questions with grading criteria

```markdown
Meta-information
================
exname: short-unique-id
extype: string
exstringtype: essay
exsolution: nil
expoints: 3
exextra[essay,logical]: TRUE
exextra[essay_format,character]: editor
exextra[essay_fieldlines,numeric]: 10
exextra[anstitle]: Title shown in ANS
```

End the solution with a criteria list. The builder moves it out of the model answer into ANS's
grading criteria and stops when the points do not add up to `expoints`.

```markdown
**Criteria**

- 0.5 pt: a probability of the data, including "or more extreme".
- 0.5 pt: conditioned on the null hypothesis being true.
```

`extype: string` without the essay fields is a short auto-scored text answer, not an open
question.

### 2.6 Data files, figures and maths

- **Data files** either sit next to the question file and are shipped with a chunk
  `include_supplement("data.csv")` plus a link `[data](data.csv)` in the text, or are linked from
  a stable website, as the examples link discoverjasp.com.
- **A static image** (`![](figure.png)`) is only shipped if it is also listed in
  `include_supplement()`. Figures drawn by an R chunk are shipped automatically.
- **Maths** goes in as `$...$` or `$$...$$`; the builder turns it into ANS's equation component.
  Plain Unicode symbols (μ, ≠, χ²) also work.
- **Tables** as markdown pipe tables. From data, use `knitr::kable()` with `results = "asis"` and
  set the column names; printing a data frame gives console lines starting with `##`.

### 2.7 Content rules

- Every wrong option is a mistake you can name (the wrong df, SD for SE, the reversed
  conditional), and the model answer names it. A distractor that can be rejected on its size
  alone is wasted.
- Every model answer ends with its source (book section and page, lecture slides), for whoever
  checks the questions.
- A calculation question ends its solution with the working. In a randomized question, write
  the working with `cat(sprintf(...))` in a chunk with `comment = ""`, from the same variables
  as the question, so it can never drift from the numbers students see.
- Say which data each part uses, label every gap, and state units and the number of decimals.
- Do not invent features of ANS, of the software students use, or of the course. Ask.

### 2.8 Markdown traps

1. A paragraph starting with `I.` becomes a roman-numeral list that swallows `II.` and `III.`;
   write `**I.**` and give each statement its own paragraph.
2. A list straight after a line of text runs into that paragraph; put a blank line before it.
3. A pipe table at the very start of the solution is not rendered; start with a sentence.
4. Inline code that starts with `r ` is run as R by knitr (`` `r = 0.80` `` breaks the build).
5. R/exams writes a key like `0.70` as `0.7`; the builder keeps the margin's decimals for the
   range, so set `extol` with the decimals you mean (`0.01`).

## 3. Building and checking

From the folder that holds `tools/`:

```sh
Rscript tools/build-ans.R <question folder> --html                 # preview only
Rscript tools/build-ans.R <question folder>                        # preview + package
Rscript tools/build-ans.R <question folder> --title-prefix="TEST " # for a trial import
Rscript tools/build-ans.R <question folder> --feedback             # practice tests
python3 tools/check-import.py <unzipped re-export> --expected <folder>/<NAME>.expected.json
```

Build the preview first and read it: labels before every gap, the stem of every tick-all
question, the source line at the end of every model answer. The full build writes `<NAME>.zip`
(import this), `<NAME>.html` (preview) and `<NAME>.expected.json` (for the check). It stops with
a message on every rule in this file it can test; fix the question, do not work around the
check.

## 4. Reading an ANS export

To convert an existing bank, the teacher exports it from ANS (**Settings > Export**) twice and
gives you both, unzipped.

**The QTI 2.X export** (a folder of XML files plus `imsmanifest.xml`) holds the complete content.

- There is one file per question, `QUE_<exercise id>_<n>.xml`. **`n` is question n of one
  multi-part exercise, not version n.** Merge the parts of an exercise; never de-duplicate them.
- The exercise title is in the manifest (`<imsmd:langstring>`) and in the item's `title`
  attribute.
- The **model answer** is a `<rubricBlock view="scorer">`, inside `itemBody` for choice and open
  questions and after `</itemBody>` for fill-in questions.
- **Question feedback** is a `<modalFeedback outcomeIdentifier="FEEDBACK" identifier="...">`
  after the rubric. `identifier` is `correct` or `incorrect`, or `choice1`, `choice2`, ... for
  feedback on one option. Teachers often keep the real explanation here rather than in the model
  answer, so read both.
- **Grading criteria** of open questions are `<rubricScoring><criterion points="0.5">`, with an
  optional description. An export may hold the points without the text.
- The **accepted answers of a gap** are every `mapEntry mapKey` of that gap's
  `responseDeclaration`. A key like `5.7;5.8` is a numeric range. Gaps often accept several values
  (both signs, comma decimals, typo variants); keep all of them.
- **Multiple-response weights** are the `mappedValue` of each option, +1/k for each of the k true
  options and -1/(n-k) for each false one. ANS does **not** recompute them when an option is
  deleted, so check them in old items.
- **Attachments** uploaded with ANS's current editor come back as `<uuid>.<ext>`, with the
  original name in `data-name`. Files of older questions, linked as
  `/redactor_images/<uuid>/download`, are **missing** from the QTI export; look them up in the
  Respondus export by that uuid.

**The Respondus export** (one `;`-separated CSV plus files) has the ANS folder of every question
(`Folder /...` tags) and the attachments, but it loses the shared scenario of multi-part
exercises and the text of fill-in questions, and it marks **every** option of a
multiple-response question as correct. Use it for folders and files only.

**The HTML in exports is messy.** Expect, and repair,

- tables with unclosed `<tr>`, nested `<th>`, merged header cells, and question text inside the
  last table cell;
- code as `<pre><code><code>line</code>...` with `<br>`s;
- `<br>` line breaks (statements I and II, two-line formulas) that become one paragraph;
- empty or unpaired `<strong>` and `<em>` around line breaks, which become stray `**` and `*`;
- zero-width spaces;
- `<` and `>` that ANS dropped from the text ("θ 0.5" for "θ > 0.5"). Restore them from the
  context, and flag them to the teacher.

Converting HTML to markdown with pandoc works once code blocks and tables are built separately.
After converting, recompute every key (rule 7): old items contain wrong keys, solutions written
for an earlier version of the numbers, and page references to older editions of the book.

## 5. Package structure

The builder writes this; it is here for debugging and for agents writing packages without it.

```
package.zip
├── imsmanifest.xml
├── QUE_10000001_1.xml        exercise 10000001, question 1
├── QUE_10000001_2.xml        exercise 10000001, question 2
├── QUE_10000002_1.xml        a single-question exercise
└── media/data.jasp, media/figure.png   (any relative path)
```

The manifest has one resource per question:

```xml
<resource identifier="QUE_10000001_1" type="imsqti_item_xmlv2p1" href="QUE_10000001_1.xml">
  <metadata>
    <imsmd:lom><imsmd:general><imsmd:title>
      <imsmd:langstring xml:lang="en">Exercise title shown in ANS</imsmd:langstring>
    </imsmd:title></imsmd:general></imsmd:lom>
  </metadata>
  <file href="QUE_10000001_1.xml"/>
  <file href="media/data.jasp"/>
</resource>
```

Inside each item, set `identifier="QUE_<id>_<n>"` and `title="<exercise title>"`. Points come
from `normalMaximum` and the `MAXSCORE` outcome; write exact values (2, not 1.999998).

## 6. Question types in QTI

### 6.1 Single choice and multiple response

A `choiceInteraction` (`maxChoices="1"` for single choice, `0` for multiple response), with the
model answer at the **end of `itemBody`**:

```xml
<itemBody>
  ...<choiceInteraction responseIdentifier="RESPONSE" shuffle="false" maxChoices="1">...</choiceInteraction>
  <rubricBlock view="scorer"><p>Model answer, with the source.</p></rubricBlock>
</itemBody>
```

Verified by import. The model answer arrives, and for multiple response the per-option weights
in the package are kept. `shuffle="false"` keeps the order written; ANS can shuffle per student
in its own settings.

### 6.2 One numeric gap

A `textEntryInteraction` with a float response and an absolute tolerance imports as an ANS
numeric gap with that margin (verified, margins 0.002 and 0.01):

```xml
<responseDeclaration identifier="R1" cardinality="single" baseType="float">
  <correctResponse><value>0.035</value></correctResponse>
</responseDeclaration>
...
<equal toleranceMode="absolute" tolerance="0.002 0.002" includeLowerBound="true" includeUpperBound="true">
  <variable identifier="R1"/><correct identifier="R1"/>
</equal>
```

ANS also has a *Numerical value* question type, but a gap shows the teacher what students typed.

### 6.3 Several gaps in one question, or several accepted answers

Use ANS's own form, as in its exports (verified by import with 5 gaps in one question: every gap
shows, but as an alphanumeric gap; see the caution in section 2.3). That
means one string `responseDeclaration` per gap, the accepted keys and a mapping **inside
`correctResponse`**, numeric margins as `low;high` keys, and the `map_response` template.

```xml
<responseDeclaration identifier="GAP1" cardinality="single" baseType="string">
  <correctResponse>
    <value>191.5</value><value>191,5</value><value>191.4;191.6</value>
    <mapping defaultValue="0">
      <mapEntry mapKey="191.5" mappedValue="0.2"/>
      <mapEntry mapKey="191,5" mappedValue="0.2"/>
      <mapEntry mapKey="191.4;191.6" mappedValue="0.2"/>
    </mapping>
  </correctResponse>
</responseDeclaration>
<!-- one per gap; only SCORE and MAXSCORE outcome declarations -->
...
<responseProcessing template="http://www.imsglobal.org/question/qti_v2p1/rptemplates/map_response"/>
```

An exact value (margin 0) gets the zero-width range `123;123` next to `123`, as in ANS's own
exports; with the plain key alone ANS made the gap alphanumeric instead of numeric (seen on
import, October 2026).
`mappedValue` is the points per gap. R/exams' own multi-gap output imports with **only the first
gap** showing; the builder rewrites it into this form.

### 6.4 Explanation of a fill-in question

ANS ignores a scorer rubric after `</itemBody>` and leaks one inside it (rule 3). The explanation
goes in as **question feedback**, the same text for a correct and an incorrect answer, after
`</itemBody>` (verified by import):

```xml
</itemBody>
<rubricBlock view="scorer"><p>For the record; ANS ignores this one.</p></rubricBlock>
<modalFeedback outcomeIdentifier="FEEDBACK" showHide="show" identifier="correct"><div>Explanation.</div></modalFeedback>
<modalFeedback outcomeIdentifier="FEEDBACK" showHide="show" identifier="incorrect"><div>Explanation.</div></modalFeedback>
<responseProcessing .../>
```

The same two feedback blocks work on choice questions (`--feedback`, for practice tests). ANS's
API (`PATCH /api/v2/questions/{id}`, field `grading_description`, personal token) could set a
fill-in's model answer directly; that route is untested.

### 6.5 Open questions with grading criteria

An `extendedTextInteraction` with `expectedLength="0"`, **no `responseProcessing`**, the model
answer as a scorer rubric at the end of `itemBody`, and the criteria after `</itemBody>`
(verified):

```xml
<rubricScoring>
  <criterion points="0.5"><div>Names the test statistic.</div></criterion>
  <criterion points="0.5"><div>Interprets the p-value as conditional on H0.</div></criterion>
</rubricScoring>
```

The criteria must add up to the question's points.

### 6.6 Multi-part exercises

Parts with the same exercise id and title, as `QUE_<id>_1.xml`, `QUE_<id>_2.xml`, ..., are
regrouped by ANS into one exercise with the parts in order (verified, including ANS's own 5-part
export re-imported). The shared scenario goes at the top of question 1.

## 7. Media, maths, links

- **Images and data files** travel inside the package, referenced by relative `src` / `href` and
  listed as `<file>` entries of their item (rule 5). They become real ANS attachments that
  students can download (verified with `.png`, `.jasp` and `.csv`).
- **Maths** goes in as `$$...$$`, which ANS turns into its equation component; MathML gets
  flattened. Tables in plain HTML are fine.
- **External links** survive. Prefer stable sites (the publisher's or the software's own pages)
  over self-hosted copies that may move.

## 8. Checking an import

After every import, the teacher exports the bank as QTI 2.X (and, if possible, as a Respondus
package) and gives you the export. Run `tools/check-import.py` on it with the build's
`expected.json`. Per question it checks

- present, with the right exercise title and number of parts;
- points;
- the model answer in the scorer rubric (choice and open questions);
- **the answer not visible in the question text** (the failure that matters most);
- feedback on fill-in questions;
- accepted keys and margins of every gap;
- the correct options and their weights;
- criteria (points and text);
- attachments present.

Report every failed check to the teacher, with what the export holds.

## 9. What the builder changes in R/exams output

R/exams (`exams2qti21()`) is a good base, but ANS needs its output reshaped. The builder
(`tools/ans_package.py`) does all of this; it matters when you debug or write packages yourself.

| R/exams writes | ANS needs |
|---|---|
| the solution as `modalFeedback` (ANS drops it) | a scorer `rubricBlock` (choice, open) or correct/incorrect feedback (fill-in) |
| a separate manifest resource per media file | `<file>` entries of the item |
| `cloze` with several float gaps | one `num` gap per question; ANS's multi-gap form (6.3) only where exact keys are fine |
| item titles "1", "2", ... | the title from `exextra[anstitle]` |
| `expectedLength="1000"` on open questions | `expectedLength="0"`, no response processing |
| MathML | `$$...$$` |

Two R/exams behaviors to keep in mind when writing questions: `expoints` in a `cloze` is per gap
(R/exams recycles it), and `exshuffle: TRUE` shuffles once at build time.

## 10. What is verified, and how

| Behavior | Status |
|---|---|
| QTI 2.1 legacy: choice and open model answers, criteria, multi-part regrouping, attachments, numeric gaps with margin | verified by import and re-export (Sept/Oct 2026) |
| Fill-in rubric inside `itemBody` leaks into the question | verified (do not do it) |
| Separate media resources create an empty exercise | verified (do not do it) |
| Correct/incorrect feedback on gaps and choice questions | verified by import, checked on screen |
| ANS multi-gap form with `low;high` ranges | every gap shows after import, but as an alphanumeric gap with the exact keys, not as a numeric gap with the range (seen October 2026) |
| Exact gaps (margin 0) | the plain key alone imports as an alphanumeric gap (seen October 2026); `123` plus `123;123` is ANS's own export form, not yet confirmed after import |
| Extra accepted keys (comma decimals, other sign) from a package | in ANS's own exports; not yet checked key by key after import |
| Per-option (`choiceN`) feedback on import | seen in exports, not tested on import |
| ANS API for fill-in model answers | untested |
| Respondus CSV import | works, but unsuitable for exams (rule 1) |
| QTI 3.0 import | loses fill-in context and model answers |
